title_en: Chengdu Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources, Wuhou Branch v. China Merchants (Shekou) Chengdu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., Chengdu Gangzhao Industrial Development Co., Ltd., and Hainan Minfeng Technology Industry Development Corporation — dispute over creditor's subrogation right
ruling_gist_en: 1. Pursuant to Article 73 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, if a debtor is idle in exercising its matured claims, thereby causing damage to the creditor, the creditor may request the People's Court to exercise the debtor's claims by way of subrogation in its own name, except where such claims are personal to the debtor. Where the debtor and the secondary debtor agree to discharge the debt by means of accord and satisfaction, and the agreement for accord and satisfaction is a real contract, then if the secondary debtor has not actually performed the accord and satisfaction, the original monetary debt between the secondary debtor and the debtor is not extinguished, and the creditor still has the right to exercise the debtor's claims by way of subrogation.

full_text_en:
Chengdu Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources, Wuhou Branch v.

China Merchants (Shekou) Chengdu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd.,

Chengdu Gangzhao Industrial Development Co., Ltd., and Hainan

Minfeng Science and Technology Industrial Development Corporation — dispute over creditor's subrogation right

【Ruling Summary】

1. Pursuant to Article 73 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, where a debtor is dilatory in exercising its matured creditor's right, thereby harming the creditor, the creditor may petition the People's Court to exercise the debtor's creditor's right in its own name by subrogation, except for creditor's rights exclusively belonging to the debtor. Where the debtor and the secondary debtor agree to discharge the debt by performance in lieu (datio in solutum), because the agreement for performance in lieu is a contract in re (real contract), if the secondary debtor does not actually perform the agreement for performance in lieu, the original monetary debt between the secondary debtor and the debtor is not extinguished, and the creditor still has the right to exercise the debtor's creditor's right by subrogation.

2. Enterprise restructuring merely transforms the organizational form and changes the economic nature of the enterprise; the enterprise's pre-existing claims and debts are not extinguished due to the restructuring. Pursuant to Article 5 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Civil Disputes Related to Enterprise Restructuring, where an enterprise, through capital increase and share expansion or partial transfer of property rights, enables others to participate in the enterprise as shareholders and wholly transforms the enterprise into a limited liability company or a joint stock limited company, the debts of the original enterprise shall be assumed by the newly established company after restructuring. Therefore, where the creditor exercises the creditor's right by subrogation against the secondary debtor, and the secondary debtor has undergone restructuring, the enterprise after restructuring shall perform the obligation of satisfaction to the creditor.

Supreme People's Court Civil Judgment

(2011) Min Ti Zi No. 210

Applicant for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Chengdu Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources, Wuhou Branch. Domicile: No. 6 Xianghe Lane, Section 3, 1st Ring Road South, Chengdu High-tech Development Zone, Sichuan Province.

Legal Representative: Gao Dou, Director of the Bureau.

Agent ad litem: Li Chunlin, lawyer of Sichuan Kangyue Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhao Shuo, lawyer of Sichuan Kangyue Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): China Merchants (Shekou) Chengdu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. Domicile: Section 4, South Renmin Road, Wuhou District, Chengdu, Sichuan Province.

Legal Representative: Wang Yun, Chairman of the Board of Directors.

Agent ad litem: Shui Bing, lawyer of Sichuan Yafeng Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Liu Yishi, lawyer of Sichuan Yafeng Law Firm.

Third Party at First Instance: Chengdu Gangzhao Industrial Development Co., Ltd. Domicile: Block 6, Dongtongshun Street District, Chengdu, Sichuan Province.

Legal Representative: He Hanguang, General Manager of the Company.

Third Party at First Instance: Hainan Minfeng Science and Technology Industrial Development Corporation. Domicile: Room 202, No. 23, Longkun North Road, Haikou, Hainan Province.

Legal Representative: Long Yuntao, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Shui Bing, lawyer of Sichuan Yafeng Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Xu Qiaorong, lawyer of Sichuan Yafeng Law Firm.

Regarding the dispute over creditor's subrogation right between the applicant for retrial, Chengdu Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources, Wuhou Branch, and the respondent, China Merchants (Shekou) Chengdu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., and the third parties, Chengdu Gangzhao Industrial Development Co., Ltd. and Hainan Minfeng Science and Technology Industrial Development Corporation, the applicant for retrial, dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2008) Chuan Min Zhong Zi No. 90 of the Sichuan High People's Court, applied to this Court for retrial. This Court, by civil ruling (2010) Min Shen Zi No. 989, decided on December 10, 2010, to bring the case up for retrial. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, with adjudicator Wang Chuang as presiding judge, adjudicator Li Jingping and acting adjudicator Wang Fubo as members. Court clerk Shang Min served as the record-keeper. The trial of this case is now concluded.

The Chengdu Intermediate People's Court, after trial, found: On June 28, 2002, the Wuhou District People's Court of Chengdu, in two cases concerning arrears of land acquisition fees owed by the Chengdu Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources, Wuhou Branch (hereinafter referred to as Wuhou Land Bureau) against Sichuan Gangzhao Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Sichuan Gangzhao Company), rendered civil judgments (2001) Wuhou Min Chu Zi No. 1924 and No. 1925, respectively. Both judgments determined: The "Debt Relationship Transfer Contract" signed on July 20, 1999, by and among the Wuhou Land Bureau, Sichuan Gangzhao Company, and China Merchants Bureau (Shekou) Chengdu Real Estate Development Company (hereinafter referred to as China Merchants Bureau Company) was a true expression of the parties' intent, its content was lawful, and it should be protected by law. Pursuant to the "Debt Relationship Transfer Contract", the debt of RMB 21,833,446.50 in land acquisition fees owed by China Merchants Bureau Company to the Wuhou Land Bureau was entirely assumed by Sichuan Gangzhao Company. Subsequently, Sichuan Gangzhao Company and the Wuhou Land Bureau signed two "Payment Contracts" on July 20, 2000, and March 29, 2001, respectively, stipulating that Sichuan Gangzhao Company should pay the Wuhou Land Bureau RMB 8 million and RMB 10 million, respectively, by September 30, 2000, and December 20, 2001, but Sichuan Gangzhao Company did not perform its payment obligation. Therefore, the Wuhou District People's Court of Chengdu, in the aforementioned two judgments, ordered Sichuan Gangzhao Company to pay the Wuhou Land Bureau RMB 10 million and RMB 8 million, respectively. After the two civil judgments became effective, the Wuhou District People's Court of Chengdu, on May 28, 2003, issued civil rulings (2003) Wuhou Min Yi Zai Zi No. 3 and No. 4, deciding to retry the two cases, and on October 15, 2003, rendered civil judgments (2003) Wuhou Min Yi Zai Zi No. 3 and No. 4, revoking the court's civil judgments (2001) Wuhou Min Chu Zi No. 1924 and No. 1925, and affirming that the "Debt Relationship Transfer Contract" signed on July 20, 1997, by and among the Wuhou Land Bureau, China Merchants Bureau Company, and Sichuan Gangzhao Company was invalid. After the judgment was pronounced, China Merchants Bureau Company, dissatisfied, appealed to the Chengdu Intermediate People's Court. That court, on December 1, 2004, rendered civil judgments (2004) Cheng Min Zai Zi No. 42 and No. 43, dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment. Thereafter, China Merchants Bureau Company further appealed to the Sichuan High People's Court. That court, on July 5, 2006, rendered civil judgments (2005) Chuan Min Zai Zhong Zi No. 41 and No. 42, revoking civil judgments (2003) Wuhou Min Yi Zai Zi No. 3 and No. 4 and (2004) Cheng Min Zai Zi No. 42 and No. 43, and affirming judgments (2001) Wuhou Min Chu Zi No. 1924 and No. 1925. The Sichuan High People's Court, in the two judgments on retrial, confirmed that the "Debt Relationship Transfer Contract" signed by the Wuhou Land Bureau, Sichuan Gangzhao Company, and China Merchants Bureau Company, and the "Payment Contracts" signed by the Wuhou Land Bureau and Sichuan Gangzhao Company were all valid contracts. At the same time, it determined that Sichuan Gangzhao Company was a company invested in and established by Chengdu Gangzhao Industrial Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Chengdu Gangzhao Company), and Chengdu Gangzhao Company failed to inject the registered capital into Sichuan Gangzhao Company as required, thus should bear liability for insufficient capital contribution. On September 1, 2006, during the enforcement of the aforementioned two cases, the Wuhou District People's Court of Chengdu issued civil rulings (2006) Wuhou Zhi Cai Zi No. 69 and No. 70, respectively, determining that Chengdu Gangzhao Company, when injecting registered capital into its established subsidiary Sichuan Gangzhao Company, failed to transfer the land use right for the Taifeng International Commercial Center project land, valued at RMB 21,441,941, which should have been invested in Sichuan Gangzhao Company, constituting insufficient capital contribution. Therefore, it ordered the addition of the third party, Chengdu Gangzhao Company, as an enforcement respondent, and Chengdu Gangzhao Company should be liable to the Wuhou Land Bureau within the scope of the insufficient registered capital of RMB 21,441,941.

Separately found: 1. China Merchants (Shekou) Import and Export Trading Company invested in establishing China Merchants Bureau (Shekou) Chengdu Industrial Development Corporation in Chengdu in 1993, and subsequently, China Merchants Bureau (Shekou) Chengdu Industrial Development Corporation invested in establishing China Merchants Bureau Company as a wholly state-owned enterprise. In 1995, China Merchants Bureau (Shekou) Chengdu Industrial Development Corporation was restructured into Chengdu Gangzhao Company. In February 1999, Chengdu Gangzhao Company invested in establishing Sichuan Gangzhao Company. In August 1999, China Merchants Bureau Company was restructured into a limited liability company and renamed as China Merchants (Shekou) Chengdu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as China Merchants Real Estate Company). During the restructuring process, Chengdu Gangzhao Company and China Merchants Bureau Company negotiated that the restructured and renamed China Merchants Real Estate Company would retain the land use right of 13,241.4 square meters of the original China Merchants Bureau Company located in Group 7, Changshou Village and Group 1, Tongzilin Village, Guixi Township, Wuhou District, Chengdu (the same plot as the Taifeng International Commercial Center project land), and simultaneously assume the debt of USD 2.3 million of the original China Merchants Bureau Company, while the remaining assets, claims, and debts would be assumed by Chengdu Gangzhao Company, and the registered capital would be increased from RMB 8 million to RMB 10 million. On August 11, 1999, Chengdu Gangzhao Company transferred all its shares in China Merchants Real Estate Company, totaling RMB 10 million, to Sichuan Qifeng Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. and two other individuals. On August 23 of the same year, China Merchants Real Estate Company was established and commenced business. On January 30, 2004, the Chengdu Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce, by "Cheng Gong Shang Chu Zi (2003) No. 06133 Penalty Decision", revoked the business license of Chengdu Gangzhao Company.

2. On April 12, 1998, Chengdu Gangzhao Company and China Merchants Bureau Company signed a "Debt and Claims Liquidation Agreement", stipulating that China Merchants Bureau Company would use the land use right for the Taifeng International Commercial Center project, covering an area of 13,241.4 square meters, valued at an appraised price of RMB 34,441,941, to be transferred to Chengdu Gangzhao Company in satisfaction of the debt of RMB 34,815,500 owed by China Merchants Bureau Company to Chengdu Gangzhao Company, thereby fully settling all claims and debts between the parties; China Merchants Bureau Company should deliver the land to Chengdu Gangzhao Company for development and use on the day after the agreement became effective. However, the land use right has not been transferred to Chengdu Gangzhao Company's name to date.

3. On November 17, 2004, Hainan Minfeng Science and Technology Industrial Development Corporation (hereinafter referred to as Hainan Minfeng Company) and Chengdu Xinda Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xinda Company) signed a "Share Transfer Agreement for China Merchants (Shekou) Chengdu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd.", stipulating that Hainan Minfeng Company would transfer its 49% shares in China Merchants Real Estate Company to Xinda Company, and that the debts of China Merchants Real Estate Company incurred before April 2003 would be borne by Hainan Minfeng Company.

Because Chengdu Gangzhao Company neither assumed the compensation liability to the Wuhou Land Bureau for insufficient registered capital nor asserted its matured creditor's right against China Merchants Real Estate Company by litigation or arbitration, thereby causing damage to the Wuhou Land Bureau's creditor's right, the Wuhou Land Bureau filed a subrogation action with the Chengdu Intermediate People's Court on November 29, 2006, requesting a judgment ordering China Merchants Real Estate Company to perform the debt of RMB 21,441,941 owed by Chengdu Gangzhao Company to the Wuhou Land Bureau, and to bear the court costs and preservation fees of this case.

The Chengdu Intermediate People's Court, after trial, held: Pursuant to the civil judgments (2005) Chuan Min Zai Zhong Zi No. 41 and No. 42 of the Sichuan High People's Court, the "Debt Relationship Transfer Contract" signed on July 20, 1999, by the Wuhou Land Bureau, China Merchants Bureau Company, and Sichuan Gangzhao Company is legally valid. According to that contract, the debt of RMB 21,833,446.50 in land acquisition fees owed by China Merchants Bureau Company to the Wuhou Land Bureau should be assumed by Sichuan Gangzhao Company. Secondly, pursuant to the aforementioned civil judgments of the Sichuan High People's Court, the civil judgments (2001) Wuhou Min Chu Zi No. 1924 and No. 1925 of the Wuhou District People's Court of Chengdu, and the civil rulings (2006) Wuhou Zhi Cai Zi No. 69 and No. 70 of the Wuhou District People's Court of Chengdu, the Wuhou Land Bureau holds a creditor's right against Sichuan Gangzhao Company in the principal amount of RMB 18 million plus interest, and Chengdu Gangzhao Company, due to insufficient capital contribution, bears liability to the Wuhou Land Bureau within the scope of RMB 21,441,941. The "Debt and Claims Liquidation Agreement" signed on April 12, 1998, between Chengdu Gangzhao Company and China Merchants Bureau Company is a true expression of the parties' intent, does not violate legal provisions, and should be legally valid. According to the terms of that agreement, China Merchants Bureau Company is obligated to deliver the land use right for the Taifeng International Commercial Center project, covering an area of 13,241.40 square meters, to Chengdu Gangzhao Company, but has not performed that obligation. After restructuring and renaming, China Merchants Bureau Company was changed to China Merchants Real Estate Company; therefore, the obligation to deliver the land use right owed by China Merchants Bureau Company to Chengdu Gangzhao Company is assumed by the restructured and renamed China Merchants Real Estate Company. Article 13 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (I) (hereinafter referred to as the Contract Law Interpretation (I)) provides: "'The debtor is dilatory in exercising its matured creditor's right, thereby harming the creditor' as stipulated in Article 73 of the Contract Law means that the debtor fails to perform its matured debt to the creditor and also fails to assert, by way of litigation or arbitration, its matured creditor's right against its debtor, which has a content of monetary payment, thereby causing the creditor's matured creditor's right to remain unsatisfied." According to this provision, one of the prerequisites for a creditor to exercise the subrogation right is that the creditor is dilatory in exercising a matured creditor's right that has a content of monetary payment, thereby causing the creditor's matured creditor's right to remain unsatisfied. In this case, the creditor's right asserted by the Wuhou Land Bureau that Chengdu Gangzhao Company holds against China Merchants Real Estate Company is a right to the delivery of land use right, not a creditor's right with a content of monetary payment. Therefore, the Wuhou Land Bureau's claim that it has the right to exercise by subrogation the creditor's right of Chengdu Gangzhao Company against China Merchants Real Estate Company does not meet the requirements for the constitutive elements of subrogation under the Supreme People's Court's Contract Law Interpretation (I), and its claim is not supported. According to Article 5 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Civil Disputes Related to Enterprise Restructuring, which provides that "where an enterprise, through capital increase and share expansion or partial transfer of property rights, enables others to participate in the enterprise as shareholders and wholly transforms the enterprise into a limited liability company or a joint stock limited company, the debts of the original enterprise shall be assumed by the newly established company after restructuring," after China Merchants Bureau Company was restructured into China Merchants Real Estate Company, all its debts should be assumed by China Merchants Real Estate Company. The court does not support the defense opinion of Hainan Minfeng Company that China Merchants Real Estate Company is not a proper respondent in this case. Regarding Hainan Minfeng Company's argument that the creditor's right held by Chengdu Gangzhao Company against China Merchants Real Estate Company has exceeded the statute of limitations, because Hainan Minfeng Company is not a party to the creditor-debtor relationship, it has no right to raise the issue of the statute of limitations. China Merchants Real Estate Company and Chengdu Gangzhao Company, having been legally summoned without justifiable reasons, failed to appear in court, and at the first instance of this case, they waived their rights to contest the facts and claims alleged by the Wuhou Land Bureau. The litigation consequences arising from the waiver of the above rights shall be borne by China Merchants Real Estate Company and Chengdu Gangzhao Company themselves. The court ruled: dismissing the claim of the Wuhou Land Bureau; court costs at first instance of RMB 117,220, and litigation preservation fee of RMB 110,520, totaling RMB 227,740, to be borne by the Wuhou Land Bureau.

The Wuhou Land Bureau, dissatisfied with the above civil judgment, appealed to the Sichuan High People's Court, arguing: The clause on "repayment by means of property in lieu" in the "Debt and Claims Liquidation Agreement" dated April 12, 1998, is invalid because it violates mandatory state regulations. According to Article 58 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Contract Law), which provides that "where a contract is invalid, any property obtained under the contract shall be returned," the creditor's right between Chengdu Gangzhao Company and China Merchants Real Estate Company remains a creditor's right with a content of monetary payment. Based on the existing evidence, the matured creditor's right has been transformed from "land transfer" into a monetary claim for return of loans and compensation. The first instance judgment, which dismissed the Wuhou Land Bureau's claim, constitutes improper application of law. China Merchants Bureau Company was a wholly state-owned enterprise. During its restructuring, it did not obtain approval from the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission, nor did it subsequently complete the approval procedures. Therefore, the "Debt, Claims, and Asset Disposition Agreement" it signed with Chengdu Gangzhao Company is invalid and should not be used as evidence. The total land price of RMB 29,448,874 stated in the "Debt, Claims, and Asset Disposition Agreement" was based on an invalid "Asset Appraisal Report", which is not legally valid and differs by more than RMB 5 million from the appraisal of the same land, raising suspicion of intentional undervaluation of state assets. The deregistration archives and the "Land Appraisal Report" of China Merchants Bureau Company lack authenticity, legality, and relevance to this case; the assertion that China Merchants Bureau (Shekou) Chengdu Industry Company was restructured into Chengdu Gangzhao Company lacks factual basis. In summary, it requests the court of second instance to revoke the original judgment and render a new judgment in accordance with the law.

China Merchants Real Estate Company argued in defense: China Merchants Real Estate Company is not a proper respondent in this case. The debtor under the liquidation agreement in question is China Merchants Bureau Company. China Merchants Real Estate Company and China Merchants Bureau Company are two different legal entities, and China Merchants Real Estate Company bears no obligation to satisfy the debts of China Merchants Bureau Company. The Wuhou Land Bureau's claim for subrogation has no legal or contractual basis. On the one hand, the right held by Chengdu Gangzhao Company under the liquidation agreement is to obtain the land use right; the Wuhou Land Bureau has no right to claim subrogation for a creditor's right that is not monetary in content. On the other hand, the Wuhou Land Bureau's debtor is Sichuan Gangzhao Company; the bureau can only exercise subrogation rights against Sichuan Gangzhao Company's debtor, and has no right to exercise subrogation rights against the creditor of Chengdu Gangzhao Company. The contractual obligation stipulated in the liquidation agreement for China Merchants Bureau Company is to deliver land to Chengdu Gangzhao Company; the Wuhou Land Bureau can only seek delivery of land, not demand monetary payment. There is no legal, certain creditor-debtor relationship between Chengdu Gangzhao Company and China Merchants Real Estate Company or China Merchants Bureau Company; those two companies are not obligated to satisfy debts. The amount of debt stated in the liquidation agreement is not authentic. According to the balance sheets of China Merchants Bureau Company and Chengdu Gangzhao Company for the same period, the total liabilities of China Merchants Bureau Company were RMB 10.79 million, and the total receivables of Chengdu Gangzhao Company were RMB 6.19 million, which differs significantly from the amount stipulated in the liquidation agreement, proving that the agreement is fraudulent. Even if the agreement were genuine, the "Debt, Claims, and Asset Disposition Agreement" signed between Chengdu Gangzhao Company and China Merchants Bureau Company would have extinguished the creditor-debtor relationship between the parties. The lawsuit filed by the Wuhou Land Bureau has exceeded the statute of limitations, and it has lost the right to win. It requests the court of second instance to dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

The grounds and requests of Hainan Minfeng Company's defense were the same as those of China Merchants Real Estate Company.

The facts found by the Sichuan High People's Court at trial, except for the relationship between China Merchants Bureau Company and China Merchants Real Estate Company, were consistent with the main facts regarding the cause and process of the dispute as found in the first instance judgment, which the court confirmed. The court further found:

1. On August 22, 1999, China Merchants Bureau Company (招商局公司) completed the "Enterprise Application for Cancellation of Registration Form," which mainly stated: the reason for cancellation was the change from wholly state-owned enterprise to a limited liability company; in the column regarding employee placement and handling of creditor's rights and debts, it was clearly stated that except for the land-related assets retained by China Merchants Real Estate Company (招商房地产公司), the remaining assets and creditor's rights and debts would all be assumed by Chengdu Gangzhao Company (成都港招公司); the loan of USD 2.3 million (equivalent to RMB 19,125,309.82) borrowed by China Merchants Bureau Company from China Merchants Bank, together with the interest accrued after June 30, 1999, would be assumed by China Merchants Real Estate Company; all other creditor's rights and debts of China Merchants Bureau Company from its establishment to August 9, 1999, would be assumed by Chengdu Gangzhao Company; it was also noted that the personnel of China Merchants Bureau Company would be placed by Chengdu Gangzhao Company.

2. On August 10, 1999, Chengdu Gangzhao Company and China Merchants Bureau Company signed the "Agreement on the Disposal of Creditor's Rights, Debts, and Assets," the main contents of which were the same as those in the aforementioned enterprise cancellation registration form.

3. China Merchants Bureau Company was a wholly state-owned enterprise approved by the Chengdu Urban and Rural Construction Management Committee on July 3, 1993, and verified by the industry and commerce authority to be invested and registered with a capital of RMB 8 million by China Merchants Bureau (Shekou) Chengdu Industrial Development Company. The company was cancelled on August 23, 1999, due to restructuring.

4. The "Balance Sheet" of Chengdu Gangzhao Company as of December 31, 1997, showed an ending balance of other receivables of RMB 6,197,415.85. The "Balance Sheet" of China Merchants Bureau Company as of December 31, 1997, showed an ending total balance of RMB 10.79 million.

5. On October 30, 2002, China Merchants Real Estate Company remitted RMB 19,056,597.56 to the China Foreign Exchange Trading Center. On November 1 of the same year, the funds were settled and exchanged for USD 2.3 million and repaid to China Merchants Bank, Chengdu Branch.

6. On August 23, 1999, China Merchants Real Estate Company's "Company Establishment Registration Application" stated that its shareholders/promoters were Sichuan Qifeng Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., Ye Wenjin, and Liu Zongming.

After trial, the High People's Court of Sichuan Province held that the main issue in dispute in this case was whether Wuhou Land Bureau (武侯国土局) could exercise the right of subrogation against China Merchants Real Estate Company.

Pursuant to the principles set forth in Article 73 of the Contract Law, which provides: "If a debtor is懈怠 (negligent) in exercising its matured claims against a third party, thereby causing damage to the creditor, the creditor may petition the People's Court to subrogate and exercise the debtor's claims in its own name, except for those claims exclusively belonging to the debtor. The scope of exercise of the right of subrogation is limited to the amount of the creditor's claim," the constitutive elements of the right of subrogation are: first, the debtor must have a claim against a third party; second, the debtor is怠于 (negligent) in exercising the claim; third, the debtor has fallen into default; fourth, damage has been caused to the creditor, and the creditor needs to preserve the claim.

The "Contract for the Transfer of Debt Relations" signed by Wuhou Land Bureau with China Merchants Bureau Company and Sichuan Gangzhao Company (四川港招公司) regarding the land expropriation fee, and the "Payment Contract" signed by Wuhou Land Bureau and Sichuan Gangzhao Company, had been confirmed as valid by the aforementioned effective judgments. Subsequently, during the enforcement of that case, the Wuhou District People's Court of Chengdu added Chengdu Gangzhao Company as the person subject to enforcement, holding it liable within the scope of RMB 21,441,941 for its insufficient registered capital in Sichuan Gangzhao Company. Based on this, it could be confirmed that Chengdu Gangzhao Company was the debtor of Wuhou Land Bureau.

Wuhou Land Bureau's claim to exercise the right of subrogation in this case was mainly based on the "Agreement on the Liquidation of Claims and Debts" signed by Chengdu Gangzhao Company and China Merchants Bureau Company. This agreement stipulated that China Merchants Bureau Company would use the land use right of the Taifeng International Trade Center project site, appraised at RMB 34,441,941, to offset its debt of RMB 34.8155 million owed to Chengdu Gangzhao Company. The claims and debts between the two parties would be settled, and China Merchants Bureau Company was required to deliver the land to Chengdu Gangzhao Company for use the day after the agreement took effect. China Merchants Real Estate Company now argued that this liquidation agreement was a false agreement signed by Chengdu Gangzhao Company to establish Sichuan Gangzhao Company, and the amount of arrears determined by the agreement lacked basic evidence to support it, but it failed to submit sufficient evidence. Based on the agreement, it could be determined that a creditor-debtor relationship existed between the two parties, i.e., China Merchants Bureau Company owed a debt to Chengdu Gangzhao Company, and it was a monetary debt. As for the agreement's provision regarding the settlement by land valuation, this was merely the method chosen by the parties to conclude the creditor-debtor relationship; whether it was lawful and valid did not affect the determination of this basic fact.

If China Merchants Bureau Company had performed the liquidation agreement as stipulated, it would no longer owe a debt to Chengdu Gangzhao Company. However, it did not actually transfer the land use right to Chengdu Gangzhao Company, so the liquidation agreement was not actually performed, and the creditor-debtor relationship between the two parties still existed. At this point, Wuhou Land Bureau could take China Merchants Bureau Company as the sub-debtor and exercise the right of subrogation in accordance with the law. However, considering all the existing evidence in this case, China Merchants Bureau Company did later undergo restructuring and was cancelled as a result of the restructuring. When China Merchants Bureau Company was deregistered, it signed the "Agreement on the Disposal of Claims, Debts, and Assets" with Chengdu Merchants Industrial Development Co., Ltd. (成都招商实业开发有限公司) concerning its claims, debts, and assets, which was recorded in the relevant registration archives of the industry and commerce authority. It was clearly stated that except for the USD 2.3 million to be repaid by China Merchants Real Estate Company on behalf of China Merchants Bureau Company, all other claims, debts, and assets would be assumed by Chengdu Gangzhao Company. The USD 2.3 million had already been repaid. Accordingly, pursuant to the "Agreement on the Disposal of Claims, Debts, and Assets," what China Merchants Real Estate Company undertook was only China Merchants Bureau Company's original financial debt to the relevant bank, which had already been performed; other claims, debts, and assets were to be borne by Chengdu Gangzhao Company itself. Since Chengdu Gangzhao Company was itself the debtor of Wuhou Land Bureau, there was no issue of exercising the right of subrogation. Although Wuhou Land Bureau now disputed the restructuring act of China Merchants Bureau Company and the related agreements, it did not submit sufficient evidence, and its claims could not be established.

China Merchants Real Estate Company was a joint-stock company approved by the industry and commerce authority and established in accordance with the standards for the establishment of a new company. It was different from China Merchants Bureau Company in terms of registered capital amount, shareholder composition, enterprise nature, etc.; the two were not simply a name-change relationship. In other words, the debt originally owed by China Merchants Bureau Company to Chengdu Gangzhao Company could not be equated with a debt owed by the current China Merchants Real Estate Company to Chengdu Gangzhao Company. The existing evidence showed that China Merchants Real Estate Company only retained the land in question from the original China Merchants Bureau Company and repaid USD 2.3 million as consideration; beyond that, it did not assume other debts of China Merchants Bureau Company, including the debt owed to Chengdu Gangzhao Company, and there was no basis for it to repay other debts on behalf of China Merchants Bureau Company. Therefore, Wuhou Land Bureau's request to treat China Merchants Real Estate Company as a sub-debtor and require it to assume the debt originally owed by China Merchants Bureau Company to Chengdu Gangzhao Company did not comply with the provisions of Article 73 of the Contract Law and the aforementioned judicial interpretation of the Supreme People's Court. The factual and legal basis for its appeal was insufficient and could not be established; the court did not support it. In accordance with Article 153, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court rendered the following judgment: the appeal was dismissed and the original judgment was affirmed. The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 117,220 was to be borne by Wohou Land Bureau.

Wuhou Land Bureau, dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of the High People's Court of Sichuan Province, applied to this court for retrial, arguing: First, the second-instance court's admission of the "Agreement on the Disposal of Claims, Debts, and Assets" signed between China Merchants Real Estate Company before its restructuring and Chengdu Gangzhao Company was erroneous. China Merchants Real Estate Company was established through the restructuring of China Merchants Bureau Company. Whether in the cancellation archives of China Merchants Bureau Company or the establishment archives of China Merchants Real Estate Company, there was no legally required approval procedure from the state-owned assets administrative department, and the appraisal unit did not possess the "Asset Appraisal Qualification Certificate" issued by the state-owned assets administrative department. The restructuring act was therefore illegal and should be invalid. The "Agreement on the Disposal of Claims, Debts, and Assets" signed during the restructuring of China Merchants Bureau Company in 1999 stated that the total appraised land price was RMB 29,448,874, while the appraised price of the same parcel of land in December 1997 was RMB 34,441,941 — a difference of more than RMB 5 million. This difference indicated that state-owned assets were intentionally undervalued during the restructuring, leading to a loss of state-owned assets. During the restructuring of China Merchants Bureau Company, the high-quality asset (the land) was transferred to the restructured China Merchants Real Estate Company, while all debts were assumed by Chengdu Gangzhao Company. This conduct itself was an act of using the opportunity of enterprise restructuring to suspend or evade debts, constituting malicious collusion that harmed the state, the applicant, and other creditors. According to Article 8 of the Supreme People's Court's "Urgent Notice on Effectively Preventing Debtors from Evading Debts in the Trial of Enterprise Bankruptcy and Restructuring Cases" (《关于人民法院在审理企业破产和改制案件中切实防止债务人逃废债务的紧急通知》), which provides: "If the parties maliciously collude to harm the interests of the state or creditors, the relevant agreement shall be confirmed as invalid," the "Agreement on the Disposal of Claims, Debts, and Assets" should be declared invalid. Second, the second-instance court's finding that China Merchants Real Estate Company should not succeed to the debts of China Merchants Bureau Company before its restructuring lacked legal and factual basis. China Merchants Bureau Company achieved the participation of others (Sichuan Qifeng Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., Ye Wenjin, Liu Zongming) in the enterprise by increasing capital and expanding shares (from registered capital of RMB 8 million to RMB 10 million) and transformed the enterprise into a limited liability company. According to Article 5 of the Supreme People's Court's "Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Civil Dispute Cases Related to Enterprise Restructuring" (《关于审理与企业改制相关的民事纠纷案件若干问题的规定》), which provides: "If an enterprise, by increasing capital and expanding shares, enables others to participate in the enterprise and transforms the whole enterprise into a limited liability company, the debts of the original enterprise shall be assumed by the new company after restructuring," the original debts of China Merchants Bureau Company should be assumed by China Merchants Real Estate Company. However, the second-instance court did not apply this judicial interpretation. China Merchants Real Estate Company acquired land worth over RMB 34 million from China Merchants Bureau Company before restructuring by assuming and repaying the loan of USD 2.3 million (i.e., RMB 19,056,597.56) from China Merchants Bank. Even if calculated at the restructured appraised value of over RMB 29 million, there was still a profit of over RMB 10 million. The original court's reasoning that "China Merchants Real Estate Company only retained the land in question from the original China Merchants Bureau Company and repaid the USD 2.3 million as consideration" as the basis for concluding that it no longer bears the debts violated the principle of debt succession and the principle that enterprise debts follow the enterprise's property changes. Third, the second-instance court's sole reliance on "registered capital, shareholder composition, and enterprise nature" to determine the relationship between China Merchants Bureau Company and China Merchants Real Estate Company, thereby concluding that "they are not simply a name-change relationship, and the debt owed by the original China Merchants Bureau Company to Chengdu Gangzhao Company cannot be equated with the debt owed by the current China Merchants Real Estate Company to Chengdu Gangzhao Company," violated the legal principle of debt succession upon enterprise changes. On August 6, 1999, the Chengdu Administration for Industry and Commerce issued a "Notice of Approval for Enterprise Name Change" to the Wuhou Administration for Industry and Commerce, stating: "The materials for the change of enterprise name registration of 'China Merchants Bureau Shekou Real Estate Company' have been received. Upon review, the change of the enterprise name to 'China Merchants Shekou Real Estate Company' is approved." This could prove that China Merchants Shekou Real Estate Company was merely a change of name during the enterprise restructuring. China Merchants Real Estate Company, when applying for a change to the "State-owned Land Use Certificate," submitted materials to the Chengdu Bureau of Land and Resources on the grounds of "name change," and the Chengdu Bureau of Land and Resources reviewed and found that "the name of the user of this parcel of land was originally China Merchants Bureau Shekou Real Estate Company, and the company name has changed to China Merchants Real Estate Company." The second-instance court's simple comparison of the two enterprises by registered capital, shareholder composition, and enterprise nature, leading to the conclusion that they were not simply a "name-change relationship," was too hasty. Since it was a state-owned enterprise restructuring, the nature and shareholder composition of the two enterprises would inevitably differ before and after. The law does not provide that if registered capital, shareholder composition, and enterprise nature have changed with industry and commerce registration, the changed enterprise will not bear the debts incurred before the change. In summary, Wuhou Land Bureau requested this court to set aside the first-instance and second-instance judgments in this case in accordance with the law, amend the judgment to support its first-instance claims, and order China Merchants Real Estate Company to bear the litigation costs and preservation fees.

China Merchants Real Estate Company responded, arguing: First, the grounds for retrial stated in the "Motion for Retrial" cannot be established. The original "Agreement on the Disposal of Claims, Debts, and Assets" was the true expression of the parties' intentions and was recorded in the industrial and commercial registration materials. Both the court of first instance and the court of second instance confirmed its validity. The retrial applicant has not yet provided any new evidence sufficient to overturn the original judgment. The second-instance court's admission of the "Agreement on the Disposal of Claims, Debts, and Assets" as evidence did not constitute an error in the application of law. The establishment process of China Merchants Real Estate Company was lawful, and there was no act of malicious collusion or debt evasion. China Merchants Real Estate Company and China Merchants Bureau Company were two independent legal persons. The creditor-debtor relationship between them had already been extinguished, and there was no issue of debt succession; each should independently assume civil liability. Second, the reasoning of the original court judgment found clear facts with sufficient and reliable evidence. The main fact found by the original judgment was that "China Merchants Real Estate Company, on the basis of taking over the land of China Merchants Bureau Company and the corresponding USD 2.3 million debt, and paying RMB 10 million in monetary funds to the original investors of China Merchants Bureau Company, was established as a joint-stock company in accordance with the standards for establishing a new company." The original judgment therefore concluded that the debt owed by the original China Merchants Bureau Company to Chengdu Gangzhao Company could not be equated with a debt owed by the current China Merchants Real Estate Company to Chengdu Gangzhao Company, and dismissed the retrial applicant's claims. The evidence supporting the main facts found by the original judgment was sufficient and reliable. Third, the original judgment correctly applied the law, and the judicial interpretation on enterprise restructuring does not apply to this case. Wohou Land Bureau cited Article 8 of the 2002 "Urgent Notice on Effectively Preventing Debtors from Evading Debts in the Trial of Enterprise Bankruptcy and Restructuring Cases" (hereinafter "Urgent Notice"), arguing that because the restructuring of China Merchants Bureau Company was not approved, the "Asset Disposal Agreement" was invalid, and thus the original judgment erred in the application of law. This view of Wuhou Land Bureau contradicts legal facts and deliberately misinterprets the law. Article 8 of the "Urgent Notice" is directed at the restructuring of state-owned enterprises. However, before 1999, China Merchants Bureau Company was no longer a state-owned enterprise, and therefore Article 8 of the "Urgent Notice" is not applicable; there is no issue of restructuring approval. The retrial applicant deliberately misinterprets the judicial interpretation on enterprise restructuring, treating the lawful act of establishing a company as an illegal act of using restructuring to evade debts. The establishment of China Merchants Real Estate Company in this case fully complied with the relevant provisions of the Company Law and the Regulations on the Registration of Companies. There was no phenomenon of transferring high-quality assets out, causing the enterprise to lose its basic production and operation capacity and its ability to repay external debts; it did not constitute an illegal act of evading enterprise debts. In summary, the retrial application of Wohou Land Bureau cannot be established, and it requests this court to dismiss the retrial application.

The response of the third-party Hainan Minfeng Company (海南民丰公司) was the same as that of China Merchants Real Estate Company.

The third-party Chengdu Gangzhao Company, after being served with the hearing notice by public announcement, did not appear in court.

Upon retrial, this court confirms the basic facts found by the courts of first instance and second instance.

This court holds that the focus of the litigation in this case is: whether Wuhou Land Bureau can exercise the right of subrogation against China Merchants Real Estate Company. This focal issue can be broken down into two specific questions: First, whether Wuhou Land Bureau can exercise the right of subrogation against China Merchants Bureau Company before its restructuring. Second, whether the restructured China Merchants Real Estate Company should bear the debts of the original China Merchants Bureau Company.

Regarding the first question, i.e., whether Wuhou Land Bureau can exercise the right of subrogation against China Merchants Bureau Company before its restructuring. This court holds that, according to Article 73 of the Contract Law, which provides: "If a debtor is negligent in exercising its matured claims against a third party, thereby causing damage to the creditor, the creditor may petition the People's Court to subrogate and exercise the debtor's claims in its own name, except for those claims exclusively belonging to the debtor," the creditor's right of subrogation is a right for the creditor to exercise the debtor's rights in its own name in order to preserve its claim from damage. In this case, the "Contract for the Transfer of Claims and Debts" signed by Wuhou Land Bureau with China Merchants Bureau Company and Sichuan Gangzhao Company, and the "Payment Contract" signed by Wuhou Land Bureau and Sichuan Gangzhao Company, have been confirmed as valid by effective legal documents of the People's Court. Wuhou Land Bureau's claim against Sichuan Gangzhao Company is legally and definitively established; therefore, Sichuan Gangzhao Company is the debtor of Wuhou Land Bureau. Chengdu Gangzhao Company, having been found by the effective judgment to have made insufficient capital contributions in the establishment of Sichuan Gangzhao Company, is held liable to Wuhou Land Bureau within the scope of the insufficient registered capital of RMB 21,441,941. Hence, Chengdu Gangzhao Company is also a debtor of Wuhou Land Bureau, and Wuhou Land Bureau's claim against Chengdu Gangzhao Company is also lawful and definitively established. On April 12, 1998, Chengdu Gangzhao Company and China Merchants Bureau Company signed the "Agreement on the Liquidation of Claims and Debts," stipulating that China Merchants Bureau Company should use the land use right of the Taifeng International Trade Center project site, appraised at RMB 34,441,941, to offset its debt of RMB 34.8155 million owed to Chengdu Gangzhao Company. This agreement was the true expression of the parties' intentions, did not violate the mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations, and should be valid. Pursuant to this agreement, China Merchants Bureau Company owed a monetary debt of RMB 34.8155 million to Chengdu Gangzhao Company, and China Merchants Bureau Company was obligated to deliver the land use right of the Taifeng International Trade Center project site to Chengdu Gangzhao Company. This court holds that the agreement between Chengdu Gangzhao Company and China Merchants Bureau Company to settle debts by land valuation constituted a legal relationship of performance in lieu (代物清偿). According to the basic principles of civil law, performance in lieu, as one of the methods of debt settlement, is a substitution of other performance for the original performance. It takes effect upon the actual acceptance of the substituted performance by a person entitled to receive it, such as the creditor. If the new debt is not performed, the original debt is not extinguished; when the new debt is performed, the original debt is simultaneously extinguished. In this case, although Chengdu Gangzhao Company and China Merchants Bureau Company signed the "Agreement on the Liquidation of Claims and Debts" and agreed to settle the debts between them by way of "using land to offset debt" as a method of performance in lieu, because the performance in lieu agreement was not actually performed, the original monetary debt of RMB 34.8155 million was not extinguished. China Merchants Bureau Company still owed a monetary debt of RMB 34.8155 million to Chengdu Gangzhao Company. Accordingly, China Merchants Bureau Company is the debtor of Chengdu Gangzhao Company and, consequently, the sub-debtor of Wuhou Land Bureau. Pursuant to Article 73 of the Contract Law and Articles 11 and 13 of the "Interpretation on the Application of the Contract Law (I)" of this court, because Chengdu Gangzhao Company neither assumed the compensation liability to Wushou Land Bureau for insufficient registered capital nor claimed the matured claim against China Merchants Bureau Company by litigation or arbitration, causing the creditor Wuhou Land Bureau's claim to fail to be realized, this constitutes "the debtor is negligent in exercising its matured claims, thereby causing damage to the creditor" as provided in Article 73 of the Contract Law. Therefore, Wuhou Land Bureau has the right to subrogate and exercise the lawful monetary claim that Chengdu Gangzhao Company had against China Merchants Bureau Company based on the "Agreement on the Liquidation of Claims and Debts." However, the scope of exercising this right of subrogation shall be limited to Wuhou Land Bureau's claim against Chengdu Gangzhao Company, i.e., within the scope of RMB 21,441,941 for insufficient registered capital.

Regarding the second issue, that is, whether the restructured Zhaoshang Real Estate Company should bear liability for the debts of the former China Merchants Bureau Company. This Court is of the opinion that the facts now established in the present case show that Chengdu Gangzhao Company had already failed to make its capital contribution to Sichuan Gangzhao Company, failing to contribute the land use right for the Taifeng International Commercial Center project, valued at RMB 21,441,941, which it should have contributed to Sichuan Gangzhao Company. Instead, on July 20, 1999, it entered into a "Debt Relationship Transfer Contract" with the Wuhou Land and Resources Bureau and Sichuan Gangzhao Company, transferring its outstanding land acquisition fee of RMB 21,833,446.5 owed to the Wuhou Land and Resources Bureau to Sichuan Gangzhao Company, a company it had established with an insufficient capital contribution. Less than one month after the signing of this "Debt Relationship Transfer Contract," on August 10 of the same year, Chengdu Gangzhao Company entered into an "Agreement on the Disposal of Claims, Debts, and Assets" with China Merchants Bureau Company, restructuring China Merchants Bureau Company into Zhaoshang Real Estate Company. It retained the land use right for the Taifeng International Commercial Center project, which should have been contributed to Sichuan Gangzhao Company, for the restructured Zhaoshang Real Estate Company, which was also responsible for repaying a loan of USD 2.3 million owed by China Merchants Bureau Company to China Merchants Bank. The remaining assets, claims, debts, and employee placement were all borne by Chengdu Gangzhao Company. On August 22 of the same year, China Merchants Bureau Company completed the "Application for Enterprise Cancellation Registration" and was cancelled on August 23 due to the restructuring. The restructuring was carried out by way of a capital increase and share expansion. Specifically, while increasing its registered capital from RMB 8 million to RMB 10 million, China Merchants Bureau Company transferred its equity interest of RMB 10 million in Zhaoshang Real Estate Company (renamed after the capital increase) to Sichuan Qifeng Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., Ye Wenjin, and Liu Zongming, thereby enabling others to participate in the enterprise and transforming the enterprise into a limited liability company. Regardless of whether the series of actions by China Merchants Bureau Company and Chengdu Gangzhao Company — including the failure to make capital contributions, the transfer of debts, the disposal of claims, debts, and assets, and the enterprise restructuring by way of capital increase and share expansion — were genuinely motivated by malicious intent to evade debts and harm the interests of creditors, the actual result was that the Wuhou Land and Resources Bureau could not realize its claims against Sichuan Gangzhao Company and Chengdu Gangzhao Company. This inevitably leads this Court to doubt the motives behind this series of actions. In order to better adjudicate civil dispute cases related to enterprise restructuring, the Supreme People's Court specifically formulated the "Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Adjudication of Civil Dispute Cases Related to Enterprise Restructuring." The principles of legal person property, enterprise debt succession, and enterprise debts following the transfer of enterprise property, as established in these Provisions, are intended to prevent the loss of enterprise property during the restructuring process and to avoid harming the interests of creditors. This Court is of the opinion that enterprise restructuring or transformation is merely a form of enterprise change. According to the principles of legal person property and enterprise debt succession, a company established after the change should succeed to the claims and debts of the original enterprise. Although China Merchants Bureau Company and Chengdu Gangzhao Company signed the "Agreement on the Disposal of Claims, Debts, and Assets" at the time of the restructuring, whether it was the debt of RMB 34,815,500 owed by China Merchants Bureau Company to Chengdu Gangzhao Company, or the loan of USD 2.3 million owed by China Merchants Bureau Company to China Merchants Bank, these were all external liabilities of China Merchants Bureau Company before the restructuring. According to the principles of legal person property and enterprise debt succession, the restructured Zhaoshang Real Estate Company should be responsible for repaying the debts of the former China Merchants Bureau Company before the restructuring. Although the restructured Zhaoshang Real Estate Company differs from the original China Merchants Bureau Company in terms of the amount of registered capital, shareholder composition, and nature of the enterprise, enterprise restructuring is merely a change in the form of organization and the economic nature of the enterprise. The claims and debts of the original enterprise are not extinguished by the restructuring. According to the principles of legal person property and enterprise debt succession, as well as Article 5 of this Court's "Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Adjudication of Civil Dispute Cases Related to Enterprise Restructuring," which stipulates that "where an enterprise, through a capital increase and share expansion, enables others to participate in the enterprise, and the enterprise is wholly transformed into a limited liability company or a joint stock limited company, the debts of the original enterprise shall be borne by the new company established after the transformation," the debts of the former China Merchants Bureau Company to Chengdu Gangzhao Company shall be borne by the restructured Zhaoshang Real Estate Company. Therefore, the Wuhou Land and Resources Bureau's request to treat Zhaoshang Real Estate Company as a secondary debtor and require it to bear the debts owed by the former China Merchants Bureau Company to Chengdu Gangzhao Company not only complies with Article 73 of the Contract Law and the provisions of this Court's "Interpretation (I) of the Contract Law" regarding the system of creditor's subrogation and its constitutive elements, but also conforms to the principles and provisions of this Court's "Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Adjudication of Civil Dispute Cases Related to Enterprise Restructuring." Therefore, the request of the Wuhou Land and Resources Bureau to require Zhaoshang Real Estate Company to bear the debts owed by the former China Merchants Bureau Company to Chengdu Gangzhao Company has a legal basis and should be supported. Zhaoshang Real Estate Company shall perform the obligation of discharging the debt within the scope of RMB 21,441,941 to the Wuhou Land and Resources Bureau. According to Article 20 of this Court's "Interpretation (I) of the Contract Law," which stipulates that "where, after trial by a people's court of a subrogation action brought by a creditor against a secondary debtor, it is determined that the subrogation right is established, the secondary debtor shall perform the obligation of discharging the debt to the creditor, and the corresponding claim and debt relationship between the creditor and the debtor, and between the debtor and the secondary debtor, shall be extinguished," after Zhaoshang Real Estate Company performs the obligation of discharging RMB 21,441,941 to the Wuhou Land and Resources Bureau, the corresponding claim and debt relationships between the Wuhou Land and Resources Bureau and Chengdu Gangzhao Company, between the Wuhou Land and Resources Bureau and Sichuan Gangzhao Company, and between Chengdu Gangzhao Company and Zhaoshang Real Estate Company (formerly China Merchants Bureau Company) shall be extinguished.

In summary, this Court is of the opinion that the claim of the Wuhou Land and Resources Bureau against Chengdu Gangzhao Company is lawful and valid, and the claim of Chengdu Gangzhao Company against the former China Merchants Bureau Company has also been confirmed by an effective legal instrument, is lawful and valid, and has become due. Chengdu Gangzhao Company neither assumed compensation liability to the Wuhou Land and Resources Bureau for its failure to make capital contributions, nor did it exercise its matured claims against China Merchants Bureau Company or the restructured Zhaoshang Real Estate Company, thereby causing the claim of the Wuhou Land and Resources Bureau to remain unsatisfied. Therefore, the retrial request and grounds of the Wuhou Land and Resources Bureau to require Zhaoshang Real Estate Company to bear the debts owed by the former China Merchants Bureau Company to Chengdu Gangzhao Company are established, and this Court supports them. The facts found in the original first and second instance judgments were basically clear, but the application of law was improper, and this Court hereby corrects them. Pursuant to Article 73 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 13, 19, and 20 of this Court's "Interpretation (I) on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China," Article 5 of the "Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Adjudication of Civil Dispute Cases Related to Enterprise Restructuring," and Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (2) and Article 186, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. The Civil Judgment (2008) Chuan Min Zhong Zi No. 90 of the Sichuan High People's Court and the Civil Judgment (2007) Cheng Min Chu Zi No. 19 of the Chengdu Intermediate People's Court are hereby reversed;

2. Zhaoshang (Shekou) Chengdu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. shall pay RMB 21,441,941 to the Wuhou Branch of the Chengdu Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources;

3. After the performance of the above payment obligation, the corresponding claim and debt relationships between the Wuhou Branch of the Chengdu Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources and Chengdu Gangzhao Industrial Development Co., Ltd., between the Wuhou Branch of the Chengdu Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources and Sichuan Gangzhao Industrial Co., Ltd., and between Chengdu Gangzhao Industrial Development Co., Ltd. and Zhaoshang (Shekou) Chengdu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. shall be extinguished.

Court costs for the first and second instances, each RMB 117,220, and litigation preservation costs of RMB 110,520, shall be borne by Zhaoshang (Shekou) Chengdu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
